title: Against wrath; self-examination; Chrysostom on daily audit
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Chrysostom urges a daily tribunal belonging toward conscience: let ye mind sit as judge over ye soul; search out faults; accuse your own vices not others'; before ye day, call conscience toward account for words, works, and thoughts. — Ye smoke belonging toward God's wrath held forth by ye law does not terrify ye one at peace: where there stands as no sin, there stands as no wrath as wages; a father's chastening does not remove ye peace belonging toward knowledge.
pass_b_english: The smoke of God's wrath held forth by the law does not terrify the one at peace: where there is no sin, there is no wrath as wages; a father's chastening does not remove the peace of knowledge.

Chrysostom urges a daily tribunal of conscience: let the mind sit as judge over the soul; search out faults; accuse your own vices not others'; before the day, call conscience to account for words, works, and thoughts.
source_text: Fumus irae Dei a lege obiectus non reformidatur a pacifico: ubi non est peccatum, non est ira ut merces; castigatio filiorum pacem scientiae non tollit. Chrysostomus monet quotidianum iudicium conscientiae: sedeat mens iudex in animam; scrutare delicta; accusata tua vitia non aliena; ante forum vocata conscientia rationem expetat verborum, operum, cogitationum.
